_sources.baseSpeedMps: Apollo planners assumed 3.6 km/h (1 m/s) for an hour-long walk-back from a failed rover (Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, 'Lunar Gaits'). Slope and surface factors slow this further. See packages/core/README.md.
_sources.maxSlopeDeg: Artemis xEVA concept of operations: walking up/down/across slopes of up to 20 deg (NASA 'EVA Lunar Surface Concept of Operations', 2020).
_sources.cautionSlopeDeg: ASSUMPTION: 15 deg, below the 20 deg suit capability; the same conops plans traverses with slopes up to ~12-16 deg, and Apollo 15 traversed ~17 deg.
_sources.bodyMassKg: Average 180 lbm (82 kg) crewmember used by Ogilvie et al., 'Mars Spacesuit Mass Requirements', ICES-2026-127.
_sources.suitMassKg: 230 lbm (104 kg) recommended starting maximum Mars suit mass (PGS + PLSS), ICES-2026-127.
_sources.gravity: Mars equatorial surface gravity 3.71 m/s^2 (Gale is at 4.8 deg S). NASA NSSDC Mars fact sheet gives 3.73 m/s^2 as the mean value; the difference is about 0.5%.
_sources.evaLimitS: BASALT analog flight rule EM6: 'A single EVA shall not exceed 6 h' (Beaton et al. 2019, Astrobiology 19(3)).
_sources.energyBudgetKJ: Exploration suits are sized for an average 1200 BTU/hr (352 W) metabolic rate (ICES-2026-127) over EVAs of up to 8 h (Artemis conops): 352 W x 8 h = 10130 kJ.
_sources.reserveFraction: BASALT flight rule EM7: plan to a <=5 h timeline plus 30 min margin inside the 6 h cap, so 1 h of 6 h (1/6) is held back.
_sources.stopDwellS: BASALT planned 30 min per sampling location (Beaton et al. 2019, Table 2).
_sources.radiationMSvPerDay: MSL RAD measured an average GCR dose equivalent rate of 0.67 mSv/day on the surface in Gale crater (Hassler et al. 2013, Science; SwRI press release).
_sources.dwellMetabolicW: ISS EVA profile average 850 BTU/hr (249 W), built from Apollo, Skylab and Shuttle data (quoted in ICES-2026-127).
